Pause at the bottom of the movement, feeling the stretch in your inner thigh.
Drive through your right heel to return to the starting position.
about: The cossack squat is a bodyweight exercise targeting the hip adductors and inner thighs. The deep lateral squat with an extended opposite leg develops hip mobility, inner thigh flexibility, and single-leg strength.

name: Skater Jump
steps: Stand on your right foot with your left foot lifted slightly off the ground.
Bend your right knee and push off explosively to jump laterally to the left.
Land softly on your left foot, swinging your right leg behind you and reaching your right hand toward your left foot.
Immediately push off your left foot and jump back to the right.
Continue alternating sides in a continuous skating motion for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The skater jump is a bodyweight plyometric exercise targeting the glutes through a lateral bounding movement. The side-to-side explosive motion develops lateral power, single-leg stability, and cardiovascular endurance.

name: Split Squat Jump
steps: Stand in a lunge position with one foot forward and one foot back.
Lower into the lunge by bending both knees to 90 degrees.
Explosively jump straight up from the lunge position.
Land softly back in the same lunge stance and immediately lower into the next repetition.
Complete the desired repetitions and switch legs.
about: The split squat jump is a bodyweight plyometric exercise targeting the quadriceps in a stationary lunge stance. Exploding vertically from the lunge develops single-leg power and challenges lower body endurance.

name: Burpee to Broad Jump
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Drop your hands to the ground and jump or step your feet back into a push-up position.
Perform a push-up, then jump your feet back toward your hands.
From a crouched position, swing your arms back and then explosively jump forward as far as possible.
Land softly with bent knees and immediately reset for the next repetition.
about: The burpee to broad jump is a full-body plyometric exercise that combines the conditioning demands of a burpee with an explosive horizontal jump. It targets the quadriceps and glutes while also developing total-body power, cardiovascular endurance, and coordination.

name: Burpee to Tuck Jump
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Drop your hands to the ground and jump or step your feet back into a push-up position.
Perform a push-up, then explosively jump your feet back toward your hands.
From a crouched position, leap vertically and drive your knees toward your chest in a tuck position.
Land softly with bent knees and immediately begin the next repetition.
about: The burpee to tuck jump is an advanced plyometric exercise combining the full-body conditioning of a burpee with an explosive vertical tuck jump. It targets the quadriceps and glutes while developing power, coordination, and cardiovascular fitness.

name: Diamond Cobra Push Up
steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands forming a diamond shape under your chest.
Lower your chest toward your hands, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
At the bottom, lower your hips to the ground and extend your arms, arching your back into a cobra stretch.
Return your hips upward and bend your elbows to lower back into the bottom of the push-up.
Push back up to the starting position.
about: The diamond cobra push up combines a close-grip diamond push-up with a cobra extension at the bottom of each rep. It targets the pectorals and triceps during the pressing phase while stretching the lower back and core through the cobra movement.

name: Lateral Walking Lunges
steps: Stand with feet together and hands on your hips or extended in front.
Step one foot out wide to the side and lower into a lateral lunge by shifting your weight over that foot.
Keep the opposite leg straight and both feet flat on the ground.
Push off the bent leg to bring your feet back together.
Repeat in the same direction for the desired steps, then switch sides.
about: Lateral walking lunges are a lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps and glutes through a side-to-side lunge pattern. They improve frontal plane strength, hip abductor activation, and dynamic balance.

name: Plank in Out
steps: Start in a forearm or high plank position with your core engaged and body in a straight line.
Jump both feet outward to a wide stance, then jump them back to the starting position.
Maintain a stable plank with your hips level throughout the movement.
Move at a consistent pace for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
about: The plank in out is a dynamic core exercise that adds a jumping component to a standard plank by moving the feet in and out. It targets the abdominals and hip flexors while elevating the heart rate and improving core stability under movement.

name: Plank T Twist
steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Lift one hand off the ground and rotate your torso, opening your chest toward the ceiling.
Extend the raised arm straight up so your body forms a T shape.
Hold for a moment, then return to the plank and repeat on the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The plank T twist is a rotational core exercise that targets the obliques by rotating from a plank position into a side plank T shape. It challenges spinal rotation, shoulder stability, and full core strength with each alternating twist.

name: Plyometric Push-ups
steps: Start in a standard push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Lower your chest toward the ground, then explosively push yourself upward.
Generate enough force to lift your hands off the ground at the top of the movement.
Land with soft elbows and immediately lower into the next repetition.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Plyometric push-ups are an explosive variation of the standard push-up that develops upper body power by requiring the hands to leave the ground. They target the pectorals with secondary emphasis on the triceps, front delts, and core through the explosive pressing motion.

name: Butt Kick (Low Impact)
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
Lift one heel toward your glutes by bending your knee, keeping your thighs parallel.
Lower that foot and repeat with the opposite leg in an alternating marching pattern.
Keep the movement controlled and low impact, avoiding jumping.
Continue for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
about: Butt kick low impact is a bodyweight cardio exercise targeting the hamstrings through a controlled heel-to-glute movement. The low-impact marching variation reduces joint stress while warming up the hamstrings and gently elevating the heart rate.

name: Crab Walk
steps: Sit on the floor with your knees bent, feet flat, and hands planted behind your hips with fingers pointing forward.
Lift your hips off the floor to enter the crab position.
Move forward or backward by coordinating opposite hand and foot movements.
Keep your hips elevated and core engaged throughout.
Continue for the desired distance or duration.
about: The crab walk is a bodyweight exercise targeting the glutes through a reverse table-top locomotion pattern. It builds hip extension strength, shoulder stability, and full-body coordination while keeping the hips elevated off the floor.

name: Dead Bug (Legs Only)
steps: Lie flat on your back with your arms flat by your sides and knees bent at 90 degrees, feet off the floor.
Press your lower back firmly into the floor and brace your core.
Slowly extend one leg toward the floor, keeping it just above the surface.
Return that leg to the bent position and extend the other leg.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The dead bug legs only is a bodyweight exercise targeting the abdominal muscles by isolating the leg extension component of the classic dead bug. Removing the arm movement allows full focus on lower abdominal engagement and spinal stability.

name: Lateral Bear Crawl
steps: Start in a bear hold position on all fours with knees hovering just above the ground.
Brace your core and move laterally by stepping your right hand and right foot out simultaneously.
Follow with your left hand and left foot to maintain your width.
Continue crawling sideways for the desired distance, then switch directions.
Keep your hips low and back flat throughout the movement.
about: The lateral bear crawl is a bodyweight exercise targeting the lats and shoulder stabilizers through sideways movement in a hovering all-fours position. It develops coordination, core stability, and shoulder endurance.

name: Side Plank Reach Through
steps: Begin in a side plank position with your elbow on the floor and body in a straight line.
Extend your top arm straight up toward the ceiling.
Rotate your torso and reach your top arm underneath your body, threading it through.
Return to the starting position with your arm extended upward.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
about: The side plank reach through is a bodyweight exercise targeting the obliques with a dynamic rotation added to the standard side plank. The reach-through motion increases thoracic rotation demand and deepens lateral core engagement.

name: Cross-body Mountain Climbers
steps: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Engage your core and drive your right knee toward your left elbow.
Return your right foot to the starting position, then immediately drive your left knee toward your right elbow.
Continue alternating sides in a controlled, rhythmic motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
about: Cross-body mountain climbers are a dynamic bodyweight exercise targeting the abs and obliques. By driving each knee to the opposite elbow, the movement adds a rotational element that intensifies core engagement and raises the heart rate.

name: Flutter Kick
steps: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and hands placed beneath your lower back for support.
Lift both legs a few inches off the ground, engaging your core.
Alternately raise and lower each leg in a small, controlled fluttering motion.
Keep your lower back pressed toward the floor throughout the movement.
Continue for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
about: The flutter kick is a bodyweight core exercise targeting the abs and hip flexors through continuous alternating leg movements. Performed lying on the back, it builds lower abdominal endurance and overall core stability.

name: Half Reverse Crunch
steps: Lie flat on your back with your hands placed beneath your lower back and legs bent at 90 degrees.
Engage your core and slowly draw your knees toward your chest, lifting your hips slightly off the floor.
Pause at the top of the movement, contracting your abs.
Slowly lower your legs back to the 90-degree starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The half reverse crunch is a bodyweight ab exercise that focuses on the lower abdominal region by curling the hips toward the chest. It provides a controlled range of motion suitable for building foundational core strength.

name: Half Sit Ups
steps: Lie flat on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor, and hands placed behind your head.
Engage your core and curl your upper body upward until your torso reaches a 45-degree angle.
Pause briefly at the halfway point, keeping your lower back in contact with the floor.
Slowly lower your torso back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: Half sit ups are a beginner-friendly bodyweight ab exercise that targets the abs through a partial range of motion. By stopping midway, the movement maintains continuous tension on the abdominal muscles while reducing strain on the lower back.

name: Plank Hip Dip
steps: Start in a forearm plank position with your elbows beneath your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Engage your core and slowly rotate your hips to the right, dipping toward the floor.
Return to the center plank position before dipping your hips to the left.
Continue alternating sides in a smooth, controlled motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
about: The plank hip dip is a bodyweight core exercise that targets the abs and obliques through controlled lateral hip rotation. Performed from the forearm plank position, it adds rotational challenge to standard plank stability, increasing oblique activation.

name: Scissor Kick
steps: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and hands placed beneath your lower back for support.
Lift both legs a few inches off the floor and engage your core.
Raise your right leg upward while lowering your left leg, then switch in a scissoring motion.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor and your legs as straight as possible.
Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
about: The scissor kick is a bodyweight core exercise that targets the abs and hip flexors through continuous alternating leg movement. It builds lower abdominal endurance and hip flexor strength while challenging core stability.

name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart.
Extend one leg straight, keeping your thighs parallel.
Engage your core and press through the heel of the grounded foot to lift your hips.
Raise your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to the raised knee.
Pause at the top, squeezing your glute, then slowly lower your hips back down.
about: The single leg glute bridge is a unilateral bodyweight exercise that targets the glutes and hamstrings through single-leg hip extension. It helps identify and correct strength imbalances between sides while improving hip stability and posterior chain strength.

name: Standard Crunch
steps: Lie flat on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor, and hands placed lightly behind your head.
Engage your core and curl your upper body off the floor toward your knees.
Pause at the top of the movement, contracting your abs.
Slowly lower your upper body back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The standard crunch is a foundational bodyweight abdominal exercise that targets the abs through spinal flexion. It is widely used as a core strength builder and can be performed by individuals of all fitness levels.

name: Standard Plank
steps: Place your forearms on the ground with elbows directly below your shoulders.
Extend your legs behind you, resting on the balls of your feet.
Align your body in a straight line from head to heels, engaging your core.
Keep your hips level and avoid sagging or raising your lower back.
Hold this position for the desired duration.
about: The standard plank is a fundamental isometric bodyweight exercise targeting the abs and core. Held on the forearms, it simultaneously engages the shoulders, lower back, and glutes, making it one of the most effective exercises for full core stability.

name: Toe Touch Crunch
steps: Lie flat on your back and raise your legs straight up perpendicular to the floor.
Extend your arms toward the ceiling.
Engage your core and reach your hands toward your feet by lifting your shoulders off the ground.
Pause at the top of the movement, contracting your abs.
Slowly lower your upper body back to the floor.
about: The toe touch crunch is a bodyweight ab exercise performed with legs vertical. Reaching toward the feet from this elevated position increases the range of motion and demands greater abdominal contraction than a standard crunch.

name: Dynamic Overhead Arm Sweep
steps: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms resting naturally at your sides.
Engage your core and maintain a straight posture.
Keeping a slight bend in your elbows, slowly sweep both arms out to the sides and upward in a wide arc.
Continue raising your arms until they are extended overhead.
Smoothly reverse the motion, sweeping your arms back down to your sides.
about: The dynamic overhead arm sweep is a bodyweight mobility exercise that targets the deltoids, chest, and upper back. By moving the arms through a wide, lateral arc to an overhead position, it actively improves shoulder joint flexibility and blood flow, making it an excellent warm-up movement.

name: Dynamic Stretch
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Swing both arms forward across your chest, then immediately swing them back out to the sides.
Continue the swinging motion in a controlled, fluid manner.
Gradually increase the range of motion over several repetitions.
Repeat for the desired duration.
about: The dynamic stretch is a movement-based warm-up exercise targeting the deltoids and upper back. Unlike static stretching, it uses momentum to increase range of motion and blood flow, making it ideal for preparing the shoulders for exercise.

name: High Plank
steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands directly below your shoulders and arms fully extended.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core, glutes, and quads to maintain a rigid position.
Avoid sagging your hips or raising your lower back.
Hold for the desired duration.
about: The high plank is a bodyweight isometric exercise targeting the abs and core while performed on extended arms. Compared to the forearm plank, it places additional demand on the shoulders and triceps, making it a versatile full-body stability movement.

name: Push Up Arm Lift
steps: Start in a standard push-up position with hands below your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Keeping your core engaged and body stable, shift your weight to your left hand.
Lift your right arm off the floor, bending your elbow and pulling your hand back alongside your torso.
Return your right hand to the starting position on the floor.
Shift your weight to your right hand and repeat the movement, lifting your left arm.
about: The push up arm lift combines a standard push-up with an alternating forward arm raise, targeting the triceps and pectorals while adding a balance challenge. The single-arm lift phase engages the core and shoulders for anti-rotation stability.

name: Cat Cow Back Stretch
steps: Start on all fours with your wrists directly under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Inhale and drop your belly toward the floor while lifting your chest and tailbone upward (cow position).
Exhale and round your back toward the ceiling, tucking your chin and tailbone (cat position).
Continue alternating between cat and cow positions in a slow, controlled rhythm.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
about: The cat cow back stretch is a bodyweight mobility exercise targeting the lower back and spine through alternating extension and flexion. It improves spinal flexibility, reduces tension, and is commonly used in warm-up and rehabilitation routines.

name: Plank to Downward Dog
steps: Start in a high plank position with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Push your hips up and back into a downward dog position, forming an inverted V shape.
Press your heels toward the floor and lengthen through your spine.
Pause at the top, feeling the stretch through your back and hamstrings.
Return to the plank position.
about: Plank to downward dog is a bodyweight mobility and strength exercise that transitions between a plank and an inverted V position. It stretches the lower back and hamstrings while strengthening the shoulders and core through the transition.

name: Prone Back Extension
steps: Lie face down on a mat with your legs extended straight back and arms extended directly in front of you.
Engage your glutes and lower back to lift your chest, arms, and legs slightly off the floor. Keep your neck neutral.
Maintain this elevated body position and slowly sweep your straight arms out to the sides and down toward your hips.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together as your hands reach your sides.
Slowly reverse the motion, sweeping your arms back forward to the starting position.
about: The prone back extension is a foundational bodyweight exercise targeting the lower back erectors through a spinal extension movement. Performed lying face down, it is commonly used in rehabilitation and warm-up routines to strengthen the posterior chain.

name: Butt Kick
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and begin jogging in place.
Increase the range of motion by kicking your heels up toward your glutes with each step.
Pump your arms in coordination with your legs.
Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement.
Continue for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
about: Butt kicks are a cardio and hamstring activation exercise performed by jogging in place with an exaggerated heel-to-glute kick. They are commonly used as a dynamic warm-up or cardio drill to engage the hamstrings and elevate the heart rate.

name: High Knee
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and begin jogging in place.
Drive your right knee upward toward your chest as high as possible.
Quickly switch legs, driving your left knee upward.
Pump your arms in coordination with each knee drive.
Continue alternating at a brisk pace for the desired duration.
about: High knees are a dynamic cardio exercise that combines running in place with exaggerated knee lifts. They engage the hip flexors and core while building cardiovascular endurance and lower body coordination.

name: Lateral Lunge
steps: Stand with feet together and hands on your hips.
Take a wide step out to your right side and bend your right knee as you lower your body.
Keep your left leg straight and your right knee tracking over your right foot.
Lower until your right thigh is parallel to the ground.
Push off your right foot to return to the starting position.
about: The lateral lunge is a bodyweight lower body exercise targeting the quads through a sideways stepping and squatting motion. It also stretches the adductors and strengthens the glutes, making it effective for developing frontal plane movement and hip mobility.

name: Place Jog
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart.
Begin jogging in place by alternating lifting each foot off the ground.
Maintain a light, bouncy rhythm on the balls of your feet.
Pump your arms naturally to match your leg movement.
Continue for the desired duration.
about: Place jogging is a simple cardio exercise performed in a stationary position. It elevates the heart rate and warms up the lower body by simulating the movement pattern of running without requiring space or equipment.

name: Plank Jack Modification
steps: Start in a high plank position with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Engage your core and jump both feet out wider than hip-width.
Immediately jump your feet back together.
Continue the in-and-out jumping motion at a controlled pace.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
about: The plank jack modification is a cardio and core exercise that combines the stability demands of a plank with the heart rate elevation of a jumping jack. By keeping the upper body fixed, it targets the shoulders and abs while conditioning the lower body.

name: Close Grip (Diamond) Push-up
steps: Start in a push-up position with your hands placed close together beneath your chest, forming a diamond with your thumbs and index fingers.
Keep your body in a straight line and engage your core.
Lower your chest toward your hands by bending your elbows.
Pause just above the floor.
Press back up to the starting position.
about: The close grip diamond push-up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the triceps with secondary pectoral involvement. The narrow hand placement intensifies triceps engagement and inner chest activation compared to a standard push-up.

name: Air Squat
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes pointed slightly outward.
Engage your core and push your hips back as you bend your knees.
Lower your body until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Keep your chest tall and your knees tracking over your toes.
Press through your heels to return to the standing position.
about: The air squat is a foundational bodyweight lower body exercise targeting the quads, glutes, and hamstrings. It teaches proper squat mechanics and builds lower body strength, making it the basis for all squat progressions.

name: Donkey Single Leg Kick
steps: Start on all fours with hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Keep your right knee bent at 90 degrees and flex your right foot.
Push your right heel upward toward the ceiling while squeezing your glute.
Pause at the top of the movement, fully contracting your glute.
Lower your knee back toward the floor without touching it.
about: The donkey single leg kick is a bodyweight glute exercise performed on all fours. By kicking one heel upward with the knee bent, it isolates the gluteus maximus and is commonly used as a glute activation exercise in warm-up and lower body routines.

name: Fire Hydrant
steps: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Keep your right knee bent at 90 degrees and lift it out to the side.
Raise your knee as high as your hip level while keeping your back flat.
Pause at the top, squeezing your outer glute.
Slowly lower your knee back to the starting position.
about: The fire hydrant is a bodyweight glute exercise performed on all fours that targets the glute medius and outer glutes through a lateral hip abduction movement. It is widely used for glute activation, hip mobility, and rehabilitation purposes.

name: Lying Leg Lift Up
steps: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and hands beneath your lower back or flat on the floor.
Keep your legs together and raise them upward until they are perpendicular to the floor.
Pause at the top, contracting your abs.
Slowly lower your legs back toward the floor without fully touching it.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
about: The lying leg lift up is a bodyweight ab and hip flexor exercise targeting the lower abdominals through a vertical leg raise. It builds lower core strength and hip flexor endurance while requiring the upper abs to stabilize the spine.

name: Skater Hops
steps: Stand on your right leg with a slight knee bend.
Push off your right foot and hop laterally to land on your left foot.
Land softly on your left foot with a bent knee to absorb the impact.
Immediately push off to the right and land on your right foot.
Continue hopping side to side in a skating motion.
about: Skater hops are a plyometric bodyweight exercise targeting the quads and glutes through explosive lateral jumping. The single-leg landing improves balance, coordination, and lateral movement mechanics while building lower body power.

name: Push-up
steps: Hands just wider than shoulders, body in a straight line.
Lower until your chest is a fist from the floor.
Push the floor away to return to the top.
about: The push-up is a foundational bodyweight exercise targeting the pectoral muscles. It simultaneously engages the triceps, shoulders, and core, making it one of the most versatile and widely used upper body exercises.

name: Plank
steps: Rest on forearms and toes with a straight body.
Brace your abs and glutes.
Log seconds held as reps.
about: The plank is a foundational bodyweight isometric exercise targeting the abs, with secondary engagement of the shoulders, lower back, and glutes. It involves maintaining a rigid straight-body position on the forearms to build core endurance, spinal stability, and full-body tension.

name: Wide Push-up
steps: Place your hands well outside shoulder width.
Lower your chest to the floor and push back up.
about: The wide grip push up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the chest with increased emphasis on the outer pectoral muscles. The wider hand position reduces triceps involvement and places greater stress on the chest, making it an effective variation for developing chest width and strength.

name: Superman
steps: Lie face-down with arms overhead.
Lift your arms, chest and legs off the floor, hold briefly, lower.
about: The superman hold is a bodyweight posterior chain exercise targeting the lower back erectors through a prone hyperextension hold. Lifting both arms and legs simultaneously engages the entire back and glutes, building spinal extension endurance.

name: Pike Push-up
steps: Get into a pike with hips high and hands on the floor.
Lower your head toward the floor between your hands.
Push back up.
about: The pike push-up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the deltoids in a vertical pressing pattern. The elevated hip position shifts the load away from the chest and onto the shoulders, making it an effective progression toward handstand push-ups.

name: Diamond Push-up
steps: Form a diamond with your hands under your chest.
Lower until your chest touches your hands, then push up.
about: The diamond push up is a bodyweight exercise targeting the chest with strong emphasis on the triceps. The close diamond-shaped hand position shifts the workload to the inner chest and upper arms, making it one of the most effective bodyweight movements for triceps development.

name: Jump Squat
steps: Squat down quickly.
Explode up into a jump and land softly.
about: The jump squat is a plyometric exercise that combines a bodyweight squat with an explosive jump. It develops lower body power, fast-twitch muscle fiber activation, and cardiovascular conditioning.

name: Pistol Squat
steps: Stand on one leg with the other out in front.
Squat down on the standing leg, then stand back up.
about: The pistol squat is an advanced bodyweight exercise targeting the quadriceps, with secondary engagement of the glutes, hamstrings, and abs. It is a single-leg squat performed to full depth while the opposite leg is held straight out, demanding exceptional unilateral strength, balance, and ankle flexibility.

name: Wall Sit
steps: Slide down a wall until your knees are at 90°.
Hold. Log seconds as reps.
about: The wall sit is a bodyweight isometric exercise targeting the quadriceps. Holding the seated wall position develops quad endurance, lower body stability, and muscular strength without any dynamic movement.

name: Glute Bridge
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips.
Squeeze at the top, then lower.
about: The glute bridge is a bodyweight exercise targeting the glutes, with secondary engagement of the hamstrings, lower back, and abs. It involves lifting the hips from a supine position to strengthen the posterior chain, improve hip extension, and stabilize the core.

name: Frog Pump
steps: Lie on your back with soles of feet together.
Thrust your hips up quickly, squeeze, lower.
about: Frog pumps are a bodyweight glute isolation exercise performed with feet together and knees flared outward. The external rotation of the hips shifts the focus to the gluteal muscles, making it an effective activation and warm-up movement.

name: Crunch
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent.
Curl your shoulders off the floor, then lower.
about: Crunches are a foundational bodyweight exercise targeting the rectus abdominis. By curling the upper body off the ground, they isolate the abdominal muscles and build core strength and endurance.

name: Bicycle Crunch
steps: Lie back with hands by your head.
Bring each elbow toward the opposite knee in turn.
about: The bicycle crunch is a bodyweight exercise that targets the abdominal muscles with a strong emphasis on the obliques. The alternating rotation and leg extension mimic a cycling motion, making it one of the most effective core exercises for muscle activation.

name: Russian Twist
steps: Sit leaning back with feet raised.
Rotate your torso side to side. Hold a weight to progress.
about: The russian twist is a classic bodyweight ab exercise that targets the obliques and core through rotational trunk movement. Performed seated with feet elevated, it challenges balance and rotational strength simultaneously.

name: Side Plank
steps: Support yourself on one forearm with a straight body.
Hold. Log seconds as reps.
about: The side plank is a bodyweight isometric exercise targeting the obliques and lateral core. Holding the body in a rigid side-lying position develops lateral stability, which is essential for spinal protection and athletic performance.

name: Dead Bug
steps: Lie on your back with arms and knees up.
Extend the opposite arm and leg, then switch.
about: The dead bug is a bodyweight core stability exercise that targets the abs while teaching proper spinal bracing. By moving opposite limbs simultaneously, it challenges coordination and deep core control while minimizing lower back stress.

name: Bird Dog
steps: On all fours, extend one arm and the opposite leg.
Hold briefly, then switch sides.
about: The bird dog is a bodyweight exercise targeting the lats and lower back, with secondary engagement of the abs and glutes. It involves alternately extending opposite arm and leg from a quadruped position to develop core stability, balance, and spinal control.

name: Mountain Climber
steps: Start in a push-up position.
Drive your knees toward your chest one at a time, quickly.
about: The mountain climber is a bodyweight cardio and core exercise targeting the abs, with secondary engagement of the shoulders, quads, and hip flexors. It involves rapidly alternating knee drives in a plank position to challenge core stability, cardiovascular endurance, and overall conditioning.

name: Lying Leg Raise
steps: Lie flat with legs straight.
Raise your legs to vertical, then lower without touching down.
about: The lying leg raise is a foundational lower abdominal exercise performed on the floor. By controlling the lowering phase, it maintains constant tension on the abs and hip flexors throughout the full range of motion.

name: V-Up
steps: Lie flat with arms overhead.
Lift your legs and torso to touch your toes, then lower.
about: The v-up, also known as a jackknife, is an advanced bodyweight core exercise that simultaneously engages the upper and lower abs. By lifting both the torso and legs together, it creates a full abdominal contraction and challenges hip flexor strength.

name: Hollow Hold
steps: Lie on your back, press your lower back down and lift arms and legs.
Hold. Log seconds as reps.
about: The hollow hold is a bodyweight isometric exercise targeting the abs, with secondary engagement of the lower back and hip flexors. It involves maintaining a curved body position with arms and legs raised off the floor, demanding sustained core compression and stability.

name: Flutter Kicks
steps: Lie on your back with legs slightly raised.
Kick them up and down in small, quick movements.
about: Flutter kicks are a bodyweight exercise targeting the abdominal muscles and hip flexors. The rapid alternating leg movement in a supine position creates sustained core tension, making it effective for lower ab endurance.

name: Burpee
steps: Drop into a push-up, touch your chest to the floor.
Jump your feet in and leap up with arms overhead.
about: The burpee is a full-body bodyweight exercise targeting the abs and cardiovascular system, with secondary engagement of the chest, quads, and shoulders. It combines a squat, plank, push-up, and jump into one continuous movement, making it highly effective for conditioning and calorie expenditure.

name: Bear Crawl
steps: On hands and feet with knees just off the floor.
Crawl forward. Log metres or seconds as reps.
about: The bear crawl is a full-body cardio and strength exercise performed in a low quadruped position. It elevates heart rate while engaging the shoulders, core, and legs simultaneously, making it an effective conditioning and functional movement exercise.
